category_title: Silent and depressed EMLLs experiencing extreme language-related frustration and school avoidance
minimal_context: Jessica and a volunteer are sitting one-on-one to read the picture book 'What Do You Do with an Idea?'
dialogue:
TUTOR: Today we are going to read the picture book 'What Do You Do with an Idea?' I want you to try reading this first page in English.

STUDENT: (Shakes her head quietly, appearing reluctant to attempt any reading in English.)

TUTOR: That's alright, I will read the book to you in English. Just listen and follow along.

STUDENT: (She remains completely silent, though her eyes are busy following the book pages and looking at your mouth and eyes while you read.)

TUTOR: I've been reading for a while now. Can you tell me what you think is happening in the story?

STUDENT: (She gives a weak smile) 그냥 이렇게 가만히 앉아있었죠. I have been sitting quietly just like this.

options.A: Ask closed-ended questions about the picture book to prompt a response from Jessica during the one-on-one reading session.
options.B: Terminate the reading demands immediately and remove the picture book from the table for 10 seconds before attempting to resume the one-on-one session.
options.C: Use frequent opportunities to respond (OTRs) throughout the reading session to maintain Jessica's orientation and engagement with the picture book.
options.D: Read the book to Jessica slowly, using both English and Korean. Read each line first in English and then in Korean, adding some Korean explanations to the author’s writing.
